recommendation_summary: Act now: keep the existing folder for drafts and add a 'Released' folder that only the three reviewers can write to. A reviewer releases a document by copying the approved file into that folder. The platform's audit logs record who copied it and when, and a retention lock keeps each released copy unchanged for seven years. The reply rejects the initials column and treats a naming convention as no control at all. No optional additions are offered. One gap remains: the reply never says the audit-log record of approver and time is itself kept for seven years, and it only asks which platform is used rather than confirming the logging and lock are available.

labels.Requirements and who asked: the customer contract requires each released document's exact approved version, approver identity and approval time to be kept for seven years, with no self-approval and no later edits to the approved version. You need this before this week's delivery.
labels.Deleted: naming convention as a control, a new document management system.
labels.Bottleneck: authors can write to the same place approvals would be recorded.
labels.Checked myself: only what you told me. I haven't seen the folder or the platform it runs on.

note: The retention lock protects the released file, but nothing says the log showing approver and time is kept for seven years.
